newsitem.title: USA: Aastrom cell producer trials started in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Aastrom cell producer trials started in Europe.

text.p: Aastrom Biosciences Inc and its strategic partner, Cobe BCT, said a European clinical trial to evaluate the use of the Aastrom Cell Production System (CPS) in the production of bone marrow stem cells has begun.

The system would be used to promote the recovery of white blood cells in breast cancer patients undergoing aggressive multiple-cycle myelosuppressive chemotherapy, Aastrom and Cobe, a unit of Gambro Group AB, said.

"This trial is designed to demonstrate the ability of Aastrom CPS produced stem cells to reduce the toxicity of multi-cycle cancer chemotherapy by restoring the blood and immune system cells that are damaged or destroyed by chemotherapy and radiation therapy," said R. Douglas Armstrong, president and chief executive of Aastrom. "Additionally, the successful production of cells from a small amount of previously frozen and stored material may expand the indications for this product."

The trial is being conducted in Marseille, France, and is the first non-clinical study of the Aastrom CPS, the companies said. Each of the patients will be infused with stem cells that are produced by hospital personnel using the Aastrom CPS.

Because the Aastrom CPS is intended to produce cells used for therapy from a small starting volume, its use is expected to be less costly and invasive than alternative stem cell collection methods, the companies said.

In addition, because the Aastrom CPS may enable the production of multiple doses of therapeutic cells from a single collection procedure, it may also permit higher and more frequent doses of chemotherapy to be administered to cancer patients, the companies said.
